intended_object: A proof-specific admissibility condition in this library's Navier–Stokes development. It says a target direction T in the plane points inward (⟪T, g/‖g‖⟫ < 0) and has a target ratio |c0·⟪T, transverse⟫/⟪T, normal⟫| below 1. I inferred this from the docstring, the section header "One target-direction parameter, with uniform mixed-point slack", and its use in `compact_target_choice`.
explanation: This structure is an internal cone condition, built from quantities local to this file: `c0`, `normalDirection`, `transverseDirection` and `targetRatio`. It exists only so that later lemmas can extract a uniform margin over a compact set (`targetRatio_continuousOn`, `compact_target_choice`). The literature has no standard object with this name and definition. It is a technical hypothesis bundled for one proof argument, so it does not formalize a recognized mathematical notion that could be checked against a textbook definition.
